content.text: Laus (German for 'Louse'), also known as 'BÃ¶se Dame' (Evil Queen) or 'Graue Laus', is a traditional German avoidance trick-taking game. Played with a 32-card German or French deck, it is a precursor to games like Hearts and Black Maria. The primary goal is to avoid capturing the Queen of Spades (the 'Louse'), which carries a heavy point penalty. Players must follow suit, aiming to dump high-value cards on their opponents.

Dates to the early 19th century in Northern Germany. It shares mechanics with the broader European family of 'Black Maria' and 'Hearts' games, which all evolved from earlier penalty trick-taking games.
Optimal for 3 or 4 players. Can be played with 2 with modifications.
32 cards (standard 52 minus 2-6). Use a Piquet or Skat deck, or remove cards 2-6 from a standard deck. No trumps.
All 32 cards are dealt out equally. For 4 players: 8 cards each. For 3 players: 10 cards each with 2 discarded (or dealt 10-11-11).

items.text: Hearts: The standard international version, typically played with full 52-card deck and all Hearts as penalty cards plus the Queen of Spades.
Black Maria: British variant with three penalty cards: Queen of Spades, Ace of Spades, and Ten of Diamonds.
Schwarzer Peter: Related children's avoidance game where the loser is the one stuck with the 'Black Peter' card.
Eff-Eff: German variant with different card point weights and additional penalty rules.
